images.title: Susie's array of coconuts
images.purpose: Put an array of coconuts in front of the student before any division fact is said: 5 rows with 7 coconuts in each row.
images.composition: One array of coconuts centred in the frame with a plain caption under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Exactly 35 coconuts in 5 rows of 7. Each coconut is one amber #E69F00 ellipse, 100 px wide and 110 px high, with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and no other mark. The column centres are at x 338, 468, 598, 728, 858, 988 and 1118 (130 px apart) and the row centres are at y 115, 245, 375, 505 and 635 (130 px apart), so the array spans x 288 to 1168 and y 60 to 690. No row, column or group is outlined, no number is shown and no bracket is drawn. Under the array, centred at x 728 and y 760, the caption Coconuts on the packing tray in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (40 px). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any number, fraction, equation, bracket or group outline drawn on the array
a number of coconuts other than 35, or rows and columns other than 5 and 7, or coconuts of different sizes
images.takeaway: The coconuts are laid out in rows and columns, an array, and the same coconuts can be counted by rows or by columns.
images.description: An array of 35 coconuts in 5 rows of 7, with a caption and no numbers.
images.context: Concept image for the hook, Susie's Array of Coconuts. It follows the idea of the opener's array in your maths book (5 rows of 7 coconuts) and writes no fact.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student count the rows and the columns, but do not say a fact on this picture. The slip to watch: counting the coconuts one by one and never seeing the rows.

image_decisions.why: The array of coconuts is the mathematics of the hook: it puts the multiplication and the two ways of splitting in front of the student without saying any fact.
